scenes.heading: Like terms and simplifying
scenes.say: Is three x squared plus two x squared equal to five x to the power of four? Lots of students think so. By the end of this video, you'll know why it isn't, and how to tidy up expressions with powers, negatives and mixed operations.
scenes.caption: Is 3x² + 2x² equal to 5x⁴? Lots of students think so. By the end of this video, you'll know why it isn't, and how to tidy up expressions with powers, negatives and mixed operations.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: $20 notes and $2 coins both show a 2, but you count them separately
scenes.science: x² and x look alike, but they are different kinds of term
scenes.breaks: x can be any number, and when x = 1, x² and x have the same value — but they are still different terms.
scenes.say: Picture a shop till with twenty-dollar notes and two-dollar coins. Both have a two on them, but you count them in separate piles. In algebra, x squared and x are like those notes and coins. They look similar, but they are different kinds of term, so they never combine.
scenes.caption: Picture a shop till with $20 notes and $2 coins. Both have a 2 on them, but you count them in separate piles. In algebra, x² and x are like those notes and coins. They look similar, but they are different kinds of term, so they never combine.

scenes.heading: Like terms
points: x²y and xy² are NOT like terms
scenes.say: Like terms have the same letters with the same powers. The order of the letters doesn't matter, so four x squared y and negative three y x squared are like terms. But x squared y and x y squared are not, because the square is on a different letter. And adding like terms never changes the power: three x squared plus two x squared is five x squared.
scenes.caption: Like terms have the same letters with the same powers. The order of the letters doesn't matter, so 4x²y and −3yx² are like terms. But x²y and xy² are not, because the square is on a different letter. And adding like terms never changes the power: 3x² + 2x² = 5x².

scenes.heading: Powers and negatives
scenes.question: Simplify 7p² − 3p + 2p² + 8p.
scenes.say: Simplify seven p squared, minus three p, plus two p squared, plus eight p. Sort the terms into piles. The p squared terms give nine p squared. The p terms: negative three plus eight is five, so five p. The answer is nine p squared plus five p.
scenes.caption: Simplify 7p² − 3p + 2p² + 8p. Sort the terms into piles. The p² terms give 9p². The p terms: −3 + 8 = 5, so 5p. The answer is 9p² + 5p.

scenes.heading: Times first, then tidy
scenes.question: Simplify 3m × 4n − 2mn + 18mn ÷ 6.
scenes.say: When operations are mixed, multiply and divide first. Three m times four n is twelve m n. Eighteen m n divided by six is three m n. Now collect: twelve, minus two, plus three is thirteen. The answer is thirteen m n.
scenes.caption: When operations are mixed, multiply and divide first. 3m × 4n = 12mn. 18mn ÷ 6 = 3mn. Now collect: 12 − 2 + 3 = 13. The answer is 13mn.

scenes.heading: Adding vs multiplying
scenes.say: Don't mix up adding and multiplying. To add, the terms must be like terms, and the power stays the same. To multiply, any terms will do, and a letter times itself becomes a square. Three x times two x is six x squared.
scenes.caption: Don't mix up adding and multiplying. To add, the terms must be like terms, and the power stays the same. To multiply, any terms will do, and a letter times itself becomes a square. 3x × 2x = 6x².

scenes.heading: Perimeter: add all four sides
scenes.say: A rectangle has two lengths of three x plus two y, and two widths of x minus y. Add all four sides and collect like terms: eight x, plus two y. So the perimeter is eight x plus two y centimetres.
scenes.caption: Two lengths of 3x + 2y and two widths of x − y. Add all four sides and collect like terms: the perimeter is 8x + 2y cm.

points: Like terms: same letters, same powers
Add coefficients; the power stays the same
Multiply and divide first, then collect
scenes.say: Quick recap. Like terms have the same letters and the same powers. Add the coefficients, and keep the power. Use your integer rules for negatives. Multiply and divide first, then collect. And check by substituting small numbers. Now try the practice questions!
